feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the experience shows clear progression, relevant tools, and solid scope. It is well written overall, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in leadership roles; this supports credibility and readiness for senior positions.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are all highly relevant and consistently presented.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with concise, action-oriented bullets and no obvious misspellings.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope. Several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would strengthen impact: e.g., engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); and keep punctuation/bullet formatting consistent, especially where bullets are embedded inline after sentences.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale, sector focus, or recent specialization.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add a sharper positioning line tied to recent work, e.g., public-sector/member association digital leadership, Drupal/CMS modernization, or enterprise content operations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, higher-impact formulation such as “multi-channel digital communications and platform strategy.”
- Consider rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, Drupal/CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated heavily elsewhere.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful, but avoid restating too many competency-list phrases from later sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and pluralize where needed: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination.”
- Shift from generic terms to higher-value leadership language: “Digital strategy & platform modernization,” “Editorial operations & workflow design,” “Analytics, reporting & performance insights.”
- Consider a tighter version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep competencies broad here; leave tools/platforms to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” and “advocacy communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with Topline Skills and Technical + IT automation/systems content.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current item with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 3–4 signature contributions that reinforce your senior positioning.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper achievement statements:
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and cross-team communications systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign/microsite experiences with modular content architecture and downloadable member toolkits.
- Delivered CMS/front-end enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties, improving usability and publishing efficiency.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, time saved, search success, or publishing speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics language overlaps with NACo Director role; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team scope, and enterprise-level ownership rather than listing channels.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with: “Directed enterprise digital communications for NACo, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production cost/time savings from the studio, reporting adoption, or governance efficiency.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video/programming language may duplicate footer projects; avoid repeating specific series names here unless tied to measurable impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than clearly showing ownership and scale. Tighten it around operational leadership, cross-functional coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Replace “helping” language with ownership verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Combine the last three bullets into one stronger outcome-focused line: “Built and scaled a weekly advocacy video update while improving editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”
- If available, add metrics such as email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the Recent Projects section; keep the emphasis here on scaling/operationalizing it, not launching it.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” also appears in the Director role; frame this item as executional leadership before later governance ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper and more differentiated by emphasizing leadership scope and public-sector specialization rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Public-sector and advocacy communications strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Stakeholder-centered content strategy” or “Content strategy and editorial planning” to sound more senior.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-based phrases or “X and Y” structures throughout.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for recent roles rather than listing broad skill labels here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Lead with **Drupal** and **CMS modernization**; they are most validated by the recent Drupal migration, microsite builds, and AI search work.
- Remove lower-evidence or lower-priority platforms from this topline line item, especially if they are not central to recent impact.
- Use broader phrasing like **front-end implementation** and **search and discovery experiences** to sound more senior and less like a software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable** already appear in “Technical + IT”; keeping all of them here creates repetition.
- **Workflow automation** also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Trim to the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger phrasing like “search, UX and content performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • Search, UX and content performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid listing every analytics tool here if they already appear in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented to reflect recent leadership-level work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider adding scale/ownership if true: “In-house studio buildout and operations” or “End-to-end livestream production for advocacy and member events”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; avoid repeating identical phrasing
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are already substantiated by the NACo studio bullet, so don’t over-expand here unless adding new specificity

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent roles emphasize Drupal-led modernization, this item should be tighter and ordered by relevance, not breadth.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider emphasizing depth with: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent impact: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise governance)” to reinforce credibility.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “CMS” or “web platforms” terminology consistently across sections.
- Consider trimming GitHub Pages if it’s not materially important to target roles; it reads lighter than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint in both sections unless one version adds context or proficiency level.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and current by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/strength signals instead of just tools, e.g. **front-end CMS implementation, lightweight scripting, deployment workflows, serverless edge functions**
- Consider a stronger version: **Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical systems: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or differentiate this section as hands-on tools only.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with **GitHub Actions**; avoid repeating both without distinction.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Good tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to a capability-led label, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent, higher-value work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; move Slack, Teams, Trello, Basecamp to the end or remove.
- If accurate, add a short qualifier to show application, e.g. “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana — used for editorial planning, cross-team coordination, approvals, and process automation.”
- Keep it concise and modernized: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Collaboration tools like Slack/Teams are low-signal unless they support a stronger systems/operations framing.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but the line is too bare to signal depth or recency. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform specificity rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add the strongest platform actually used most recently first; ordering can imply recency/relevance.
- Consider clarifying enterprise use where true: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise email journeys)** • **Higher Logic Thrive Marketing** • **Mailchimp**
- Keep naming consistent with other technical lists: avoid slashes unless part of official product name; use official product branding.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in NACo roles; don’t add generic descriptors like “email marketing” here unless tied to a distinct capability.
- If Higher Logic was central in NACo work, consider naming it in a recent role bullet instead of expanding this skills line further.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger NACo entries above it. Make this role more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you specify what changed.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements, rather than repeats, the stronger digital/media accomplishments in later NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business value: supported policy/program teams, translated research into member-facing content, etc.
- Split into 2 concise bullets and emphasize ownership verbs: launched, produced, supported, developed.
- Add measurable detail if available: number of episodes, audience, stakeholder groups served, or types of multimedia/content produced.

Suggested edit
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production to expand the organization’s multimedia communications.
- Supported innovation and research initiatives for program and policy teams, helping translate county-focused research into digital and multimedia content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Avoid broad “oversaw production” language already used in more senior later roles.
